Батарея на 11 000 мА·ч, прошлогодний Snapdragon и камера на 200 Мп: Honor представила геймерский смартфон Magic 9 Super Edition
28.09.2026
[17:02],
Николай Хижняк
Компания Honor представила в Китае флагманский игровой смартфон Magic 9 Super Edition. В основе устройства используется мощный чип Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. Новинка получила мощную основную камеру и батарею огромной ёмкости.

Источник изображений: Honor
Honor Magic 9 Super Edition оснащён 6,81-дюймовым LTPS OLED-дисплеем с разрешением 2788 × 1280 пикселей, частотой обновления 120 Гц, поддержкой HDR, пиковой (локальной) яркостью 10 000 кд/м
2
(глобальная яркость 2000 кд/м
2
) и высокочастотной ШИМ-регулировкой яркости (3840 Гц) и узкими рамками шириной 1,03 мм.
Аппарат получил 50-Мп фронтальную камеру и блок из трёх основных камер на задней панели, включающий основной 200-Мп сенсор Samsung S5KHP5 размером 1/1,55 дюйма, сверхширокоугольную камеру на 12 Мп (оптика f/2.4) и 50-Мп телеобъектив (оптика f/2.4) Sony LYTIA с фокусным расстоянием 500 мм и 3-кратным оптическим зумом. Задняя камера может снимать видео в 4K при 120 кадрах в секунду, фронтальная — в 4K при 60 кадрах в секунду.
Honor Magic 9 Super Edition оснащен чипом обработки изображений Honor H1 и поддерживает телеконвертер G200.
Смартфон может похвастаться очень ёмким аккумулятором на 11 000 мА·ч, созданным по технологии Qinghai Lake. Батарея содержит 25 % кремния и обладает плотностью энергии 963 Вт·ч/л, что обеспечивает повышенную надёжность и увеличенный срок службы устройства. Для новинки заявлена поддержка быстрой зарядки мощностью 80 Вт (стандарты 80 Вт PPS и 40 Вт UFCS), а также беспроводной зарядки мощностью 50 Вт и реверсивной зарядки на 27 Вт.
В составе процессора Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite пятого поколения используются два ядра с частотой 4,6 ГГц и шесть ядер с частотой 3,62 ГГц. В числе других особенностей новинки отмечаются движок Phantom Engine 3.0, оперативная память LPDDR5X, накопитель UFS 4.1, чип Honor RF Enhancement C3, а также система охлаждения, включающая вентилятор Honor Dongfeng Turbine (скорость работы — 30 тыс. об/мин) и испарительную камеру Honor Jade Plate 2.0. По словам компании, система охлаждения на 30 % эффективнее отводит тепло от рабочих компонентов.
Толщина устройства составляет 8.1 мм, а вес — 227 граммов. Смартфон будет предлагаться в чёрном, зелёном, жёлтом и белом цветах исполнения.
Honor Magic 9 Super Edition уже доступен для предзаказа в Китае. Базовая конфигурация устройства с 12 Гбайт ОЗУ и 256 Гбайт постоянной памяти оценивается в 4500 юаней (около $670). В продаже также будут доступны конфигурации с 16 Гбайт оперативной и до 1 Тбайт постоянной памяти.

Американская ИИ-компания Anthropic презентовала новую экономичную модель искусственного интеллекта Claude Sonnet 5.5, которая работает на 30% быстрее предшественницы и приближается по возможностям к флагманским решениям. Об этом сообщает «Хайтек» со ссылкой на Anthropic.
Разработчики спроектировали Claude Sonnet 5.5 как сбалансированное решение для программирования, анализа документов, создания презентаций и проектирования интерфейсов. Новинка выполняет задачи значительно эффективнее и тратит до 30% меньше вычислительных токенов по сравнению с базовой версией Sonnet 5.
В тестах на написание программного кода нейросеть набрала 70,6%, показав колоссальный отрыв от прошлой модификации с ее 10,3%. В ряде профессиональных испытаний ИИ практически сравнялся по результатам с премиальной моделью Opus 5.5, но стоимость ее использования для клиентов осталась в два раза ниже.
Создатели также значительно улучшили зрение ИИ и способность воспринимать сложные графические данные. Во время внутренних испытаний Claude Sonnet 5.5 успешно прошла культовую видеоигру Pokémon Red, ориентируясь исключительно по скриншотам виртуального экрана. Из-за резко возросшей мощности инженеры сразу оснастили алгоритм строгими протоколами безопасности и защитой от массового извлечения внутренних данных конкурентами. Доступ к новой нейросети уже открыли на всех основных облачных платформах и через официальный API компании.

Anthropic upgrades Claude with new Sonnet 5.5 model, details here
Zac Hall
| Sep 28 2026 - 11:07 am PT
0 Comments
Anthropic is upgrading Claude Sonnet, replacing Sonnet 5 from June with Sonnet 5.5 as the best medium-sized model.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 upgrades Anthropic’s medium model
Anthropic currently offers a few AI models under the Claude umbrella.
The three main models are Haiku (smallest and cheapest), Sonnet (medium size and price), and Opus (largest and most expensive of the three).
There’s also Fable/Mythos, which is even more capable and costly, which represents Anthropic’s highest tier.
Today’s new Claude model follows the arrival of Opus 5.5
last week
. Anthropic promised to upgrade Sonnet and Haiku “in the coming weeks” at the time.
Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in the Claude 5.5 family.
It’s a clear upgrade over Sonnet 5, runs more than 30% faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work.
pic.twitter.com/UvXD8mDTF1
— Claude (@claudeai)
September 28, 2026
Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 is strongest at everyday tasks with a clear scope, including fixing bugs and creating polished documents, slides, and spreadsheets.
The company also highlights its design capabilities, from refining user interfaces to producing slides that follow templates and need minimal editing.
Early testers described it as a better collaborator than Sonnet 5, Anthropic says, with clearer writing and speed suited to quick iteration on less complex tasks.
Sonnet 5.5 is now live in Claude Code! 🎉
https://t.co/bU5dcnKQyl
— Lydia Hallie ✨ (@lydiahallie)
September 28, 2026
Sonnet 5.5 keeps Sonnet 5’s pricing: $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million cache reads.
Anthropic says it typically uses far fewer tokens to complete the same work, while generating output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5, making it the fastest Sonnet model to date.
With cybersecurity capabilities comparable to Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5 is the first Sonnet model to launch with cyber safeguards and fallbacks similar to those used for Anthropic’s most capable models.
Its biology safeguards remain unchanged from Sonnet 5. Anthropic says both target a narrow set of high-risk requests, leaving routine software development and most life sciences work unaffected.

OpenAI has apologised to Australians for its
agent attack on Medicare
, and will front parliament next week as the tech company revealed more details about its June hack of Australian government websites.
Ministers on Tuesday evening released a brief, five paragraph email which
OpenAI
used to inform the Australian government about the attack. The email was sent to a public inbox monitored by Services Australia on 10 September – nearly three months after the AI agent accessed the website on 18 June – and was signed off with the closing “best”.
The Labor government has publicly voiced its fury at the manner in which OpenAI disclosed the incident. The email itself, obtained by Guardian Australia, advised Services Australia that “an OpenAI model identified a way to make the server carry out instructions sent through the public reporting interface, without a private account or password”.
In a
blog post
released on Tuesday morning (Aest), OpenAI said it should have handled its response better.
“We also should have handled our response better. We are sorry and working to do better in the future.”
The company also provided more detail on the incident
revealed by the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese
, last week.
OpenAI said it became aware of agent activity on Australian government websites in mid-August after the company reviewed earlier training incidents after the
Hugging Face attack
in July.
The agents gained non-public access to a Services Australia portal for Medicare statistics, and OpenAI said the agent was able to run commands, retrieve internal files, credentials, and write files, but no patient or client records were accessed.
12:23
Rogue AI hacks government system for first time - The Latest
OpenAI’s email to Services Australia pointed the government to the “affected URL”, a Medicare statistics page on the human services website, as well as specifying an “affected report” – a CSV file, commonly used for spreadsheets.
“We recommend that the team responsible for the service investigate the vulnerability and assess the changes needed to prevent it. We would be glad to brief your security team and provide supporting evidence as available,” OpenAI wrote.
“Best, OpenAl Security Team”.
OpenAI was contacted for comment.
The NSW Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research’s public crime mapping tool was also accessed, with application configuration, operational jobs and logs and website metadata provided to the agency.
The agent discovered an exposed access key to query the Victorian agency for health information’s reporting system to access aggregate survey statistics.
For the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, OpenAI agents retrieved aggregate statistics, but separate attempts to bypass access controls were unsuccessful and the information obtained was publicly available.
Services Australia and the Victorian health department were informed on 10 September, while the NSW bureau of crime stastistics was informed on 18 September.
The Australian Institute of Health and Welfare was not informed until 24 September, as OpenAI deemed it did not meet disclosure thresholds.
“Since then we’ve worked closely with Australian government agencies to share what we’ve learned to date,” OpenAI said. “If we identify any additional affected agencies, we will notify them promptly and directly with the information available and provide updates as further facts emerge.”
The incident occurred after one model was tasked to research government spending per person on medicines for skin conditions in Victoria. The model had difficulty obtaining that information, and OpenAI said “it took actions that we had not authorised it to take” including accessing Services Australia’s Medicare statistics reporting service.
OpenAI hack on Australian government reveals anxiety at heart of global artificial intelligence dilemma
Read more
OpenAI said it would commit resources and expertise to affected agencies, and provide Australian government agencies with support to build cyberdefences on critical infrastructure.
Australian government agencies and industries will also be given credits out of OpenAI’s US$1bn (AU$1.4bn) Daybreak fund, which lets those organisations use frontier AI for cyberdefence, and to harden their systems by reviewing code and system configurations for potential vulnerabilities that can then be patched.
The company said it would also establish a taskforce with Australian expertise to develop practical policy recommendations on managing risk with AI agents.
OpenAI’s chief strategy officer, Jason Kwon, will appear at the joint select committee on AI on Tuesday 6 October. Guardian Australia
reported on Monday
that Anthropic would also appear at this hearing, but not at a Senate inquiry into AI and datacentres this week.
Albanese, who was in the United States last week when he announced the hack, said at the time he had spoken with OpenAI’s chief executive,
Sam Altman
, “to express Australia’s extreme concern about this incident”.
On Tuesday, Albanese said OpenAI had been “very constructive and open in engaging” since the incident, as had Anthropic. He said AI can improve economic growth and productivity but it also carries risks.
“And we’ve seen those risks exposed – not just in what occurred in Australia, but the revelation that has occurred in the United States and other countries as well.”
The federal government has flagged it could introduce mandatory reporting rules for AI-related data breaches, after the revelation OpenAI used
a public-facing email address
three months after the hack to report the incident to Services Australia.
The company said on Tuesday it had “a lot of work ahead” to rebuild trust with Australians but said it was making “meaningful changes”.

title: OpenAI ‘sorry and working to do better’ after hack of Medicare and other Australian government websites

Artificial intelligence firm to front parliament as it apologises to Australians for agent attack

OpenAI has apologised to Australians for its agent attack on Medicare, and will front parliament next week, as the tech company revealed more details about its June hack of Australian government websites.

In a blog post released on Tuesday, OpenAI said it should have handled its response better.
